questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bhutan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bhutan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bhutan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.proof: The country is bordered on the south by the Republic of India and on the north by China.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Bhutan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Bhutan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.proof: The currency is the Ngultrum, which is pegged at par with the Indian rupee.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Indian state of Sikkim separates Bhutan and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Bhutan”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.proof: The Indian state of Sikkim separates Bhutan and Nepal.
